newsitem.title: USA: PSE&G sees rate cut with securitization.
newsitem.headline: PSE&G sees rate cut with securitization.

text.p: Public Service Electric and Gas Co can cut rates five percent with the securitization of its stranded assets, Fredrick D. DeSanti told Reuters.

But the legislation to allow the sale of the bonds will probably be delayed by this year's state and gubernatorial elections, he said Wednesday. DeSanti is the utility's director of state government affairs.
He does expect the legislature to pass a law phasing out the state's 13.5 percent gross receipts tax despite the election.

The tax change and asset securitization are the two legislative actions needed to implement the New Jersey Energy Master Plan proposed by the state's Board of Public Utilities last month, DeSanti said.
Although 1997 is an off year for elections in most of the United States, New Jersey elects a Governor and all members of both houses of the Legislature.
The chances of a tax change "look very good," DeSanti said, pointing out that the Governor's budget includes no revenues from the gross receipts tax.
If the tax law is not changed, DeSanti said: "I cannot see how any large customer could stay with us" once they are able to buy power from out of state.
With securitization of stranded assets, PSE&G "can do a five percent reduction" of rates right away, DeSanti said. The utility is a subsidiary of Public Service Enterprise Group Inc.
He said PSE&G stands to benefit more than GPU Inc.

Securitization provides greater immediate impact when stranded assets are investments in plant that is not retaining its value rather than in future power purchases from non-regulated generators, the source of most of GPU's stranded assets, DeSanti explained.
Other utilities operating in New Jersey are Orange & Rockland Utilities Inc and Atlantic Energy Inc.
He declined to say how much PSE&G will seek to securitize, saying that amount will not be determined until the utility prepares the filing required on July 15 by the Energy Master Plan.
He noted that securitization will speed up recovery of PSE&G's stranded costs, explaining the plans in New Jersey call for a 10-year bond, while the utility now depreciates assets over 16 years.
The pending proposals call for the tax to be phased out over six or seven years and replaced with the State's six percent sales tax and nine percent corporate income tax, he said.
The sales tax will be collected on all energy sales, not just those by electric and natural gas distribution utilities.
He said this will reduce taxes on utilities to about 7.5 percent of revenues from the present 13.5 percent.
